coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 only (140 bpm ceiling). Your recovery score is 46/100 and resting HR is elevated 7 bpm above 30-day avg—that's a flag. Yesterday's 10-miler at 129 avg plus the 19-miler last week means your CNS is still fatigued. This is taper week 21, not peak week 19; the goal is *retention*, not stimulus. Keep it conversational, sub-threshold. Dial back the mental intensity—no temptation to 'test your legs.' The mountains will wait 17 days.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're in taper, not calorie deficit. Eat at maintenance or +5–10% above normal: your glycogen stores need to be full, and sub-threshold runs don't burn enough to warrant cutting carbs. Aim for 6–8g carbs per kg body weight daily (assuming 75kg, that's 450–600g). Your sleep efficiency is 70%—slightly low. Post-run today, consume 1.2g carbs + 0.3g protein per kg within 30 min, then a full meal 2–3 hours later. Hydration: 0.5–0.7L per hour on the run; electrolytes if you're over 90 min.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is adequate in duration (8.3h) but 70% efficiency suggests fragmented sleep or early waking—likely anxiety or elevated cortisol from training load. Prioritize sleep hygiene tonight: no screens after 21:00, dark room, cool temp (16–18°C), aim for 90-min sleep cycles (7.5–9h). Consider a 15–20 min nap post-run if travel allows. Elevated resting HR + moderate recovery score = mild parasympathetic suppression. One easy week won't fix that, but refusing harder stimulus today will prevent digging the hole deeper.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 17 days out with a moderately suppressed recovery picture. Resist the urge to 'make sure you're still fit'—that's ego, not strategy. Alpine ultras are won in the descent and on nutrition discipline, not in the final taper days. Visualize the Kranjska Gora course: steep tech downhills, sparse aid, cold. Your job now is sleep, easy running, full glycogen, and mental rehearsal. Trust the 32 weeks of work. The sharpness will come from rest, not one more hard session.
